title: "Changelog"

---

This is the changelog for the **ImmPrint collection**, the curated data itself. It
is versioned independently of the [`immprintr`](https://akmclz.github.io/immprintr/)
R package that delivers it. Each released collection snapshot is immutable;
new curation ships as a new version.

## 0.3.0-alpha {#sec-0-3-0-alpha}

*Re-tiers genes by transcriptional causality, renames the first tier, adds
`readout_type` and narrows both apoptosis sets.*

- Tier 1 is renamed **Input**. It holds the most upstream node in a set, which is a
  receptor in most sets and a driving transcription factor in the MHC, proliferation
  and metabolic sets, where the Receptor label was wrong.
- **88 memberships change tier.** A gene is now placed by where its transcript sits in
  the response. The transducer tier claims a transcript is constitutive, and many
  genes sitting there were induced outputs.
- Induced negative feedback moves to the effector tier: `SOCS1`, `SOCS3`, `CISH`,
  `USP18`, `TNFAIP3`, `NFKBIA`, `NFKBIZ`, `TNIP3`, `BCL3`, `AXIN2`, `DTX1`, `BIRC3`,
  `CFLAR`, `SMAD7`, `SKIL` and `IL13RA2`. This reverses the 0.2.0 placement of
  `TNFAIP3` and `NFKBIA`, which were tiered by where their proteins act. Both are
  NF-κB target genes whose transcripts track TNF pathway activity.
- The rule is transcriptional induction, not inhibition. `AXIN1`, `BIRC2`, `XIAP`,
  `SKI`, `SMAD6`, `IRF9`, `TREX1` and `ENPP1` are constitutive negative or standing
  regulators and stay at the transducer tier.
- Induced transcription factors and kinases move to the effector tier: `IRF1`, `IRF8`
  and `CIITA` in IFNG, `IRF7` in IFNA/IFNB, `TBX21` in IL12, `GATA3` in IL4/IL13,
  `PRDM1` and `BCL6` in IL21, `CEBPB` in IL17, `ZEB1` in TGFB and `PIM1` in CSF2.
- Tiers are set-relative. A master regulator is a transducer in the set it defines and
  an effector in the set that induces it, so `CIITA`, `GATA3`, `TBX21` and `FOXP3`
  each hold two tiers.
- Chemokine receptors that mark a polarised state move from Input to Effector:
  `CXCR3` and `CCR5` (Type 1), `CCR4`, `CCR8` and `PTGDR2` (Type 2), `CCR6` (Type 17)
  and `CTLA4` in the regulatory set. All sit downstream of the master TF, so tiering
  them as inputs inverted those sets. Receptors for the polarising cytokines stay at
  Input.
- **New column `readout_type`**, placed after `regulatory_role`. It records what a
  score over the set means: `inducible` where the effector tier reads out activity
  (32 sets), `state` where the set describes a differentiation state and all tiers
  should be scored (6 sets) and `machinery` where the score reflects standing
  apparatus with no activity claim (6 sets).
- The metabolic sets were tiered by position in metabolite or electron flux, which
  carries no information in transcript space because their genes are co-regulated.
  `HIF1A` and `PPARA` become Inputs with their target regulons at the effector tier.
  `PPARGC1A`, `NRF1` and `TFAM` become Inputs, and the eighteen ETC and ATP-synthase
  subunits collapse to one transducer tier.
  `IMMPRINT_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION` has no effector tier and is `machinery`, since
  nothing in the transcriptome reads out respiratory flux.
- **`IMMPRINT_APOPTOSIS_INTRINSIC` narrows from 22 to 8 memberships** and becomes an
  apoptotic priming set of the transcriptionally dynamic BCL2 family. Execution
  machinery and the post-translationally regulated BH3-only proteins are removed,
  along with `TP53`, whose transcript stays flat whatever p53 is doing. Single-cell QC
  discards high-mitochondrial-fraction cells, so genes reporting on execution report
  on a population that has already been filtered out.
- **`IMMPRINT_APOPTOSIS_EXTRINSIC` narrows from 15 to 6 memberships**: `FAS`,
  `TNFRSF10A`, `TNFRSF10B`, `CASP8`, `CASP10` and `CFLAR`. `TNFRSF1A`, `TRADD`,
  `FADD`, `BIRC2`, `BIRC3` and `BID` duplicated `IMMPRINT_TNF_SIGNALLING`.
- 23 memberships are removed and none added. The column order is `gene_set,
  gene_symbol, pathway_level, regulatory_role, readout_type, cell_type, pmids,
  reference_gene_set`. The collection holds **44 gene sets** and **697** memberships.
- `IMMPRINT_COMPLEMENT_PRODUCTION` is unchanged and carries
  `readout_type = machinery` as a holding value. Its tiers encode the complement
  cascade, which runs extracellularly across cells. It is slated for removal in
  0.4.0-alpha.

## 0.2.0-alpha {#sec-0-2-0-alpha}

*Adds a regulatory role annotation, replaces many animal-only citations with human ones and extends
cell type to multiple lineages.*

- New column **`regulatory_role`**, placed after the signalling tier
  (`pathway_level`) and before `cell_type`. It records each gene's effect on its
  *own* pathway: `none` for a forward component or output, `inhibitory` for a
  negative regulator, `activating` for genuine positive feedback, and
  `context_dependent` where the sign varies.
- Citations were reassessed to replace animal-only foundational
  references with verified human pathway-explicit primary sources wherever a clean
  one exists. 83 memberships had their PMID set revised; where no clean human
  primary exists the foundational reference is kept.
- `cell_type` now records multiple lineages per membership where the biology
  warrants, `;`-delimited (for example `Epithelial; Fibroblast`), and refinement
  rows that previously duplicated a gene across lineages are consolidated into a
  single multi-value row.
- The inhibitory checkpoints PD1 and CTLA4 are stamped `T cell` across their
  receptor and transducer tiers, and IL7 is likewise restricted to `T cell`
  throughout, since its receptor is lymphoid-restricted and human IL7R loss of
  function spares B and NK cells. IL15 is restricted to `T cell; NK cell`, its
  responder lineages. `IL15RA` is removed, since the high-affinity chain is
  expressed by the trans-presenting myeloid or stromal cell and not the
  responder, and ImmPrint records genes expressed by the responding cell.
  Cytolytic effectors are `T cell; NK cell`. 55 memberships had their cell type
  revised.
- `CD80` and `CD86` are removed from `IMMPRINT_CTLA4_SIGNALLING`. They are the B7
  ligands on the antigen-presenting cell and not components of the T-cell
  signal, so they sit outside a signalling set on the same grounds costimulatory
  molecules are excluded from MHC class II.
- `TNFAIP3` (A20) and `NFKBIA` (IκBα) are added to `IMMPRINT_TNF_SIGNALLING` at the
  transducer tier with `regulatory_role = inhibitory`. Both are TNF-induced, but
  they enter as components and not as induced outputs, because each acts back on
  the cascade itself.
- `MCL1` is added to `IMMPRINT_IL7_SIGNALLING` at the effector tier, joining `BCL2`
  as an IL-7 driven survival output. Both cite the same human primary, which shows
  IL-7 sustaining Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 through STAT5 in human T cells.
- `GZMB` is removed from `IMMPRINT_IL21_SIGNALLING`. Cytotoxic granule effectors
  stay in `IMMPRINT_CYTOLYTIC_ACTIVITY` and are not duplicated into the
  cytokine signalling sets that prime them.
- `FASLG` is removed from `IMMPRINT_CYTOLYTIC_ACTIVITY`. It kills through the Fas
  death-receptor pathway and not granule exocytosis, so it falls outside the
  granule-mediated scope of the set. The KLR recognition receptors are retained as
  the recognition step that precedes degranulation.
- `GATA3` is added to `IMMPRINT_IL4_IL13_SIGNALLING`.
- `CXCL8`, `CCL2` and `IL6` are added to `IMMPRINT_IL1_SIGNALLING`, and `S100A8`
  to `IMMPRINT_IL17_SIGNALLING`, all at the effector tier. Each is an inflammatory
  output induced through the named pathway in human cells.
- `CSF2` (GM-CSF) is added to `IMMPRINT_IL2_SIGNALLING` and
  `IMMPRINT_IL12_SIGNALLING` at the effector tier and not to
  `IMMPRINT_IL23_SIGNALLING`. In human T helper cells GM-CSF is induced by IL-2
  through STAT5 and promoted by the IL-12 driven Th1 axis while the IL-23 axis
  constrains it, reversing the expectation set by mouse pathogenic-Th17 models.
- Two accidental duplicate rows are removed from `IMMPRINT_IL17_SIGNALLING`:
  `CXCL8` and `DEFB4A` each held a `pan` row alongside a lineage-scoped row for
  the same gene. The pan rows are kept with their citations merged, restoring the
  rule that a gene appears once per set.
- The column order is `gene_set, gene_symbol, pathway_level, regulatory_role,
  cell_type, pmids, reference_gene_set`. The collection now holds **44 gene sets**
  and **720** memberships.

## 0.1.0-alpha {#sec-0-1-0-alpha}

*First public snapshot.*

- **44 gene sets**, **724** gene set memberships.
- Every membership carries at least one PubMed citation.
- Each gene is placed in the three-tier Receptor, Transducer, Effector signalling
  hierarchy.
- Cell type structure: a cell type-agnostic `pan` core per pathway, with effector
  refinements layered on for specific lineages (listed below).
- MSigDB corroboration (Hallmark, Reactome, GO:BP) recorded per membership in
  `reference_gene_set` where applicable.
- Antigen-receptor and inhibitory-checkpoint pathways (TCR, BCR, CTLA4, PD1) are
  restricted to their defining lineage and terminate at the transducer tier by design.

### Cell type variant genes

The genes added beyond each pathway's `pan` core, by responding lineage. TCR and
BCR carry no `pan` core, so the genes shown there are the full lineage-restricted set.

**`IMMPRINT_BCR_SIGNALLING`**

- *B cell*: CD79A, CD79B, LYN, SYK, BTK, BLNK, PLCG2, PIK3CD, PIK3R1, AKT1, CARD11, BCL10, MALT1, NFATC1, NFKB1, RELA, VAV1

- *Monocyte/Macrophage*: FCGR1A, IL12B, CYBB

**`IMMPRINT_IL10_SIGNALLING`**

- *Monocyte/Macrophage*: CD163, TIMP1, NFIL3, FCGR3A, MERTK

**`IMMPRINT_IL17_SIGNALLING`**

- *Epithelial*: DEFB4A, S100A7, CCL20, CXCL8, LCN2, CXCL1
- *Fibroblast*: IL6, CXCL8, CSF3, CXCL1, CCL20

**`IMMPRINT_IL4_IL13_SIGNALLING`**

- *B cell*: FCER2, IGHE, IGHG4, IL4I1
- *Epithelial*: MUC5AC, CLCA1, POSTN, SERPINB2, CAPN14

- *T cell*: IL21, BCL6, ICOS

**`IMMPRINT_TCR_SIGNALLING`**

- *T cell*: CD3D, CD3E, CD3G, CD247, LCK, FYN, ZAP70, LAT, LCP2, PLCG1, ITK, PRKCQ, CARD11, BCL10, MALT1, NFATC1, NFKB1, RELA, VAV1

**`IMMPRINT_TGFB_SIGNALLING`**

- *Epithelial*: SNAI1, VIM, SNAI2, CDH2, FN1

**`IMMPRINT_TNF_SIGNALLING`**

::: callout-note
The `alpha` label signals that the collection is still growing and that definitions
and citations may change between alpha snapshots. Pin the version you use, and cite
it (see [Cite](cite.qmd)). The first non-alpha release will freeze a stable
baseline.
:::
